paludohadros:table:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (table of new taxa)

paludohadros:study:1.title: A new iguanodontian dinosaur from the Weald Clay Formation (Lower Cretaceous) of Smokejacks Brickworks, southern England (Journal of Systematic Palaeontology, 2026)

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered during a field trip on July 22, 2001, at the Smokejack Clay Pit near Ewhurst in Surrey, UK.
facts.quote: On July 22, 2001, the British Geologists' Association conducted a field trip to Smokejack Clay Pit (now Ewhurst Works) near the village of Ewhurst in Surrey, UK.

facts.statement: Geoff Toye discovered the partial skull and skeleton of Paludohadros approximately 100 meters west of the site where the spinosaurid Baryonyx walkeri was found.
facts.quote: Geoff Toye discovered a partial iguanodontian skull and skeleton in the same rock layer that produced the Baryonyx specimen, albeit around 100 m west.

facts.statement: Ricardo J. Sacamoto and colleagues formally described Paludohadros proudlovii as a new genus and species in 2026, designating specimen NHMUK PV R 16396 as the holotype.
facts.quote: In 2026, Ricardo J. Sacamoto and colleagues described Paludohadros proudlovii as a new genus and species of hadrosauroid dinosaur based on these fossil remains, designating NHMUK PV R 16396 as the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Four humeri and four tibiae from Smokejack Pit, originally described by W. H. E. Rivett in 1953 and 1956, were later referred to Paludohadros.
facts.quote: Four humeri and four tibiae from Smokejack Pit, described by W. H. E. Rivett in 1953 and 1956, were referred to this species.

facts.statement: Paludohadros lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Barremian age.
Fossils of Paludohadros are known from the Weald Clay Formation and likely the Wessex Formation in the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Paludohadros () is an extinct genus of hadrosauroid ornithopod dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian age) Weald Clay Formation and likely also the Wessex Formation of the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The genus Paludohadros contains the single species P. proudlovii, known from a partial skull, skeleton, and various isolated remains.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Paludohadros proudlovii, known from a partial skull and skeleton, as well as various isolated remains.

facts.statement: Paludohadros is estimated to have reached a length of about 5 meters.
facts.quote: Paludohadros is estimated to have been about 5 m long.

facts.statement: Paludohadros is distinguished from other iguanodontians by features such as ridges on lower jaw teeth, a dorsal projection on the surangular bone, a proximal ridge on the humeral condyle, a posteroventrally curving ischium with a boot, and bosses on the proximal tibia.
facts.quote: The skeleton of Paludohadros is distinguished from other iguanodontians by several anatomical characters, including the number of ridges on the teeth of the lower jaw, a well developed upward (dorsally) projecting lateral process (extension) of the surangular bone of the lower jaw, the distal condyle of the humerus having ridge that projects proximally (towards the body), the ischium curves backwards and downwards (posteroventrally) and has a well developed boot, and a tibia with bosses (growths) on the (proximal) end closest to the knee joint.

facts.statement: Paludohadros is classified as a hadrosauroid ornithopod dinosaur.
Phylogenetic analysis places Paludohadros as a non-hadrosauromorph hadrosauroid.
facts.quote: A phylogeny conducted by the studies describing authors found Paludohadros to be a non-hadrosauromorph hadrosauroid.

facts.statement: A 2021 review suggested that the remains initially identified as Iguanodon might actually belong to the genus Mantellisaurus.
facts.quote: In a 2021 review of Smokejacks fossils, these "Iguanodon" remains were instead regarded as belonging to the related genus Mantellisaurus.

rejected.statement: An initial report in October 2001 identified the remains as belonging to a juvenile Iguanodon.
rejected.quote: An initial report by the Geologists' Association in October, 2001 identified the remains as belonging to a juvenile Iguanodon.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'identified the remains as belonging to a juvenile'

rejected.statement: The authors of the 2026 study suggested that a surangular bone from the Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight likely belongs to Paludohadros.
rejected.quote: The studies authors also suggested a surangular bone (NHMUK PV R 105a) from an unknown locality of the Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight was likely attributable to Paludohadros.
